newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat futures end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat futures end sharply higher.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed sharply higher after European officials said they were suspending subsidized wheat exports until July, traders said.
The action should boost demand for U.S. wheat and lift prices, traders said. Also, the USDA weekly export report showed better-than-expected U.S. wheat exports this past week.
USDA today said U.S. wheat sales the week ended April 10 totaled 263,900 tonnes, above expectations for 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes, and up five percent from the previous week.
Commercials were on both sides of the market.
Wilson Trading bought 2.5 million bushels of July and Garnac bought 1.3 million, traders said..
Country Hedging sold 1.0 million and Atwood Larson was a net seller of 400,000 of July and 500,000 September.
MGE wheat closed up 16-1/4 to 20-3/4 cents, with July up 19-1/2 at $4.51-1/2 per bushel. MGE wheat was trading with a 30-cent daily limit after closing with limit gains Monday.
MGE May barley closed down three cents at $6.57 per cwt.
Estimated volume was 34.924 million bushel in spring wheat and 34 lots of barley.
